title: Fancy Zones interferes with dropdown overlays in Adobe Creative Cloud apps

judgment.rationale: The enabled-and-zoned versus disabled comparison, exact Adobe versions, screenshots and ZIP support direct reproduction. Related discussion supplies an auto-placement/popup-setting discriminator, not proof the issue is already fixed.
evidence: Reported on 0.81.0 after a 0.74-era change, affecting Bridge workspace/content dropdowns and InDesign point-size dropdowns.
The dropdowns work with FancyZones disabled and fail when enabled with the app placed in a zone; Photoshop and Illustrator were not affected in the original report.
#29197 records a maintainer reproduction and workaround involving popup snapping plus moving new windows to their last zone.
#46879 reports Adobe issues on 0.97.2 and was closed into #33108.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce Adobe transient-window placement and trace which automatic zoning path moves or hides the dropdown.

fix_assessment.rationale: Related issues establish a useful failure family but no issue-specific merged implementation was found. Existing popup filters must be tested rather than assumed absent.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Adobe transient dropdowns out of automatic zone restoration
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a transient Adobe dropdown is classified or restored as a normal zoned window, moving it away from its anchor or interfering with visibility. A classification mismatch or a restoration path bypassing eligibility are competing causes.
plan: Reproduce with the Adobe parent zoned and record the new dropdown HWND, owner, styles, original bounds and automatic placement events.
Trace FancyZones automatic new-window/last-zone handling and DefineWindowType; correct only the path that demonstrably admits or moves the transient overlay.
Add regression coverage for the captured dropdown predicate and restoration sequence while retaining legitimate owned-dialog snapping and excluding menus/tooltips.
verification: Bridge workspace/content dropdowns and InDesign point-size lists remain visible and anchored with FancyZones enabled and the parent zoned.
Compare automatic move-to-last-zone on/off and child-window snapping on/off.
Verify normal app restoration, Outlook dialogs and Edge menus are not regressed.

confidence.rationale: A maintainer reproduced the related popup/auto-placement interaction and a later Adobe report maps here, but the current failing event path was not traced.

issue_context.summary: Adobe Bridge and InDesign dropdown overlays disappear when their parent is zoned with FancyZones enabled; disabling FancyZones restores them.
known_information: The report provides Bridge 14.1 GA/prerelease and InDesign 19.4 versions, screenshots and a PowerToys diagnostic archive.
The original reporter runs PowerToys without elevation.
The sole issue comment is automated similarity matching.
A later Adobe 0.97.2 report was explicitly deduplicated into this issue; that is not a merged fix.
inferences: Transient-window automatic placement is a plausible common mechanism, but rendering failure versus displaced bounds must be distinguished.
Current filtering already excludes some popups, so a blanket claim that all dropdowns are accepted would be unsupported.
issue_context.analysis: Use the public test steps and known settings discriminator for maintainer reproduction rather than requesting more screenshots or the already attached ZIP.
initial_investigation: Read the entire report and sole comment and exhausted the timeline; inspected #29197, #29350 and #46879.
In #29197, the maintainer says no bug report is needed because it is reproducible and identifies the popup/last-known-zone combination; the reporter confirms the workaround.
Inspected FancyZonesWindowProcessing.cpp at main commit 3d6827a53a579ba9bedcf8d4bbda21348d78cbdb; current popup filtering explicitly mentions excluding Edge menus.
No Adobe UI test or archive-content analysis was performed.

reproduce.title: Compare Adobe dropdowns with automatic restoration toggled
reproduce.version_requirement: Current supported PowerToys and Adobe builds; reported baselines are PowerToys 0.81.0, Bridge 14.1 and InDesign 19.4.
prerequisites: A licensed Adobe test installation with Bridge or InDesign, a simple zone layout and a test profile.
Record current FancyZones settings and restore them after testing.
steps: 1. With FancyZones disabled, open Bridge workspace/content dropdowns or the InDesign point-size list as a baseline.
2. Enable FancyZones, zone the parent and repeat the same dropdown.
3. Toggle moving newly created windows to their last known zone, then child-window snapping, one setting at a time.
4. Capture dropdown bounds, visibility, owner/root, styles, classification and automatic movement events before and after creation.
5. Verify any correction against a normal new zoned window and a non-snappable popup menu.
reproduce.expected_result: Dropdowns remain attached to their controls and visible; ordinary automatic restoration still works for eligible top-level windows.
